Born and raised in [[Pilar, Buenos Aires]], Colapinto began competitive [[kart racing]] at the age of nine, winning several regional and national championships. Graduating to [[junior formulae]] in 2018, Colapinto won his first title at the [[2019 F4 Spanish Championship]] with [[Drivex]]. He then finished third in the [[2020 Formula Renault Eurocup|Formula Renault Eurocup]] and the [[2020 Toyota Racing Series|Toyota Racing Series]] in 2020. Colapinto moved into [[sportscar racing]] in 2021, competing in the [[LMP2]] class of the [[2021 FIA World Endurance Championship|FIA World Endurance Championship]], [[2021 European Le Mans Series|European Le Mans Series]] and [[2021 Asian Le Mans Series|Asian Le Mans Series]] for [[G-Drive Racing|G-Drive]], finishing third at the latter. He also contested [[2021 Formula Regional European Championship|Formula Regional European]] with [[MP Motorsport|MP]], finishing sixth overall. Colapinto progressed to [[FIA Formula 3]] in {{FIAF3|2022}}, finishing fourth the [[2023 FIA Formula 3 Championship|following season]] with [[MP Motorsport|MP]] and graduating to [[FIA Formula 2]]. A member of the [[Williams Driver Academy]] from 2023 to 2024, Colapinto made his Formula One debut with [[Williams Racing|Williams]] at the [[2024 Italian Grand Prix]], replacing [[Logan Sargeant]] for the remainder of the {{F1|2024}} season as an interim for the incoming [[Carlos Sainz Jr.]] With his debut, he became the [[Formula One drivers from Argentina|first Argentine driver]] to compete in Formula One since [[Gastón Mazzacane]] in {{F1|2001}}. Colapinto scored his maiden points finish at the {{F1GP|2024|Azerbaijan}}, repeating this feat in the [[2024 United States Grand Prix|United States]]. He joined [[Alpine F1 Team|Alpine]] as a reserve driver for {{F1|2025}} and was promoted after six Grands Prix to replace [[Jack Doohan]], where he achieved a season-best result of eleventh at the {{F1GP|2025|Dutch}}. Colapinto is contracted to remain at Alpine until at least the end of the 2026 season. ==Early and personal life== Franco Alejandro Colapinto was born on 27 May 2003 in [[Pilar, Buenos Aires]], Argentina. Colapinto is of [[Italian people|Italian]] descent through his father and of [[Ukrainian people|Ukrainian]] descent through his mother, Andrea Trofimczuk;{{cite news|url=https://setantasports.com/uk/racing/novachok-f1-franko-colapinto-maie-ukrainske-korinnia/|title=Новачок Ф1 Франко Колапінто має українське коріння|language=uk|publisher=setantasports.com|date=11 September 2024}} he is a dual citizen of Argentina and Italy.{{cite news |date=19 September 2024 |title=La nacionalidad de Colapinto |trans-title=The nationality of Colapinto |url=https://www.lagaceta.com.ar/nota/1052154/opinion/cartas-lectores-nacionalidad-colapinto.html |publisher=[[La Gaceta (Spain)|La Gaceta]] |language=Spanish}} Colapinto's father, Aníbal, was part-owner of [[Turismo Carretera]] team JC Competición in the 2010s.{{cite news|url=https://www.solotc.com.ar/franco-colapinto-tc-infancia-papa-equipo/|title= Franco Colapinto y su infancia junto al TC|publisher=SoloTC|date=27 April 2026|language=es}} Colapinto's favourite drivers are [[Lewis Hamilton]] and [[Ayrton Senna]], and his favourite [[racing circuit]] is [[Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps|Spa-Francorchamps]].
